1. Try to instantiate a Link component without explicit arguments (passing None or no values)
2. Expect the component to be created with None defaults that can be updated later
3. Currently this likely fails or doesn't behave as expected

### 1.5 Best Practices

- Add appropriate warnings when None values are used
- Make minimal changes to existing functionality
- Ensure proper testing of the new behavior

    98	Introduction
    99	============
   100	
   101	The oemof.solph package is part of the
   102	`Open energy modelling framework (oemof) <https://github.com/oemof/oemof>`_.
   103	This an organisational framework to bundle tools for energy (system) modelling.
   104	oemof-solph is a model generator for energy system modelling and optimisation.
   105	
   106	The ``oemof.solph`` package is very often called just ``oemof`` as it was part of the
   107	oemof meta package. Now you need to install ``oemof.solph`` instead of ``oemof``, but
   108	everything else is still the same.
   109	(Note: Since the oemof package refers to legacy versions before v0.4,
   110	it is not possible to install both, oemof and oemof.solph, at the same time.
   111	Just use ``pip install oemof.solph``.)
   112	
   113	Everybody is welcome to use and/or develop oemof.solph.
   114	Read our `contribution <https://oemof.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing.html>`_ section.
   115	
   116	Contribution is already possible on a low level by simply fixing typos in
   117	oemof's documentation or rephrasing sections which are unclear.
   118	If you want to support us that way please fork the oemof repository to your own
   119	github account and make changes as described in the `github guidelines <https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/quickstart/hello-world>`_
   120	
   121	If you have questions regarding the use of oemof you can visit the forum at `openmod-initiative.org <https://forum.openmod-initiative.org/tags/c/qa/oemof>`_ and open a new thread if your questions hasn't been already answered.
   122	
   123	Keep in touch! - You can become a watcher at our `github site <https://github.com/oemof/oemof>`_,
   124	but this will bring you quite a few mails and might be more interesting for developers.
   125	If you just want to get the latest news, like when is the next oemof meeting,
   126	you can follow our news-blog at `oemof.org <https://oemof.org/>`_.
   127

Use the `project site <https://readthedocs.org/projects/oemof>`_ of oemof.solph to choose the version of the documentation. Go to the `download page <https://readthedocs.org/projects/oemof/downloads/>`_ to download different versions and formats (pdf, html, epub) of the documentation.

   133	.. _installation_label:
   134	
   135	Installation
   136	============
   137	
   138	If you have a working Python3 environment, use pypi to install the latest oemof version. Python >= 3.6 is recommended. Lower versions may work but are not tested.
   139	
   140	
   141	::
   142	
   143	    pip install oemof.solph
   144	
   145	If you want to use the latest features, you might want to install the **developer version**. The developer version is not recommended for productive use::
   146	
   147	    pip install https://github.com/oemof/oemof-solph/archive/dev.zip
   148	
   149	
   150	For running an oemof-solph optimisation model, you need to install a solver.
   151	Following you will find guidelines for the installation process for different operation systems.
   152	
   153	.. _windows_solver_label:
   154	.. _linux_solver_label:
   155	
   156	Installing a solver
   157	-------------------
   158	
   159	There are various commercial and open-source solvers that can be used with oemof.
   160	There are two common OpenSource solvers available (CBC, GLPK), while oemof recommends CBC (Coin-or branch and cut).
   161	But sometimes its worth comparing the results of different solvers.
   162	Other commercial solvers like Gurobi or Cplex can be used as well.
   163	Have a look at the `pyomo docs <https://pyomo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/solving_pyomo_models.html#supported-solvers>`_ to learn about which solvers are supported.
   164	
   165	Check the solver installation by executing the test_installation example below (see section Installation Test).
   166	
   167	**Linux**
   168	
   169	To install the solvers have a look at the package repository of your Linux distribution or search for precompiled packages. GLPK and CBC ares available at Debian, Feodora, Ubuntu and others.
   170	
   171	**Windows**
   172	
   173	 1. Download `CBC <https://github.com/coin-or/Cbc/releases>`_
   174	 2. Download `GLPK (64/32 bit) <https://sourceforge.net/projects/winglpk/>`_
   175	 3. Unpack CBC/GLPK to any folder (e.g. C:/Users/Somebody/my_programs)
   176	 4. Add the path of the executable files of both solvers to the PATH variable using `this tutorial <https://www.computerhope.com/issues/ch000549.htm>`_
   177	 5. Restart Windows
   178	
   179	Check the solver installation by executing the test_installation example (see the `Installation test` section).
   180	
   181	
   182	**Mac OSX**
   183	
   184	Please follow the installation instructions on the respective homepages for details.
   185	
   186	CBC-solver: https://projects.coin-or.org/Cbc
   187	
   188	GLPK-solver: http://arnab-deka.com/posts/2010/02/installing-glpk-on-a-mac/
   189	
   190	If you install the CBC solver via brew (highly recommended), it should work without additional configuration.
   191	
   192	
   193	**conda**
   194	
   195	Provided you are using a Linux or MacOS, the CBC-solver can also be installed in a `conda` environment. Please note, that it is highly recomended to `use pip after conda <https://www.anaconda.com/blog/using-pip-in-a-conda-environment>`_, so:
   196	
   197	.. code:: console
   198	
   199	    conda install -c conda-forge coincbc
   200	    pip install oemof.solph
   201	
   202	
   203	.. _check_installation_label:
   204	
   205	Installation test
   206	-----------------
   207	
   208	Test the installation and the installed solver by running the installation test
   209	in your virtual environment:
   210	
   211	.. code:: console
   212	
   213	  oemof_installation_test
   214	
   215	If the installation was successful, you will receive something like this:
   216	
   217	.. code:: console
   218	
   219	    *********
   220	    Solver installed with oemof:
   221	    glpk: working
   222	    cplex: not working
   223	    cbc: working
   224	    gurobi: not working
   225	    *********
   226	    oemof.solph successfully installed.
   227	
   228	as an output.

   239	Citing
   240	======
   241	
   242	For explicitly citing solph, you might want to refer to
   243	`DOI:10.1016/j.simpa.2020.100028 <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.simpa.2020.100028>`_,
   244	which gives an overview over the capabilities of solph.
   245	The core ideas of oemof as a whole are described in
   246	`DOI:10.1016/j.esr.2018.07.001 <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esr.2018.07.001>`_
   247	(preprint at `arXiv:1808.0807 <https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.08070v1>`_).

   253	Examples
   254	========
   255	
   256	The linkage of specific modules of the various packages is called an
   257	application (app) and depicts for example a concrete energy system model.
   258	You can find a large variety of helpful examples in `oemof's example repository <https://github.com/oemof/oemof-examples>`_ on github to download or clone.
   259	The examples show optimisations of different energy systems and are supposed
   260	to help new users to understand the framework's structure.
   261	There is some elaboration on the examples in the respective repository.
   262	The repository has sections for each major release.
   263	
   264	You are welcome to contribute your own examples via a `pull request <https://github.com/oemof/oemof-examples/pulls>`_ or by sending us an e-mail (see `here <https://oemof.org/contact/>`_ for contact information).
